failure_summary: render_decision mislabels the opponent half as the player s own: alias you-key-line = windows:c2r1,c3r1,c4r1,c5r1 with role “the whole four-in-a-row line you are playing for” is board-false (visualize_board 44443 shows c4r1 and c5r1 are BOTH Green/P1 discs, so player 2 can never make four there), and the L2 text “let the opponent occupy c2r1, completing their double threat” names the wrong square — on the engine’s own finalMovestring 4444332 the opponent occupies c3r1 at move 7 and c2r1/c6r1 are the two resulting gravity-top winning squares; both runs faithfully echoed both render errors.
notes: n_runs=2 (this run has 2 runs per case, not 5), so no axis was sub-sampled away — A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 were graded on both runs; A1/A2/A6 copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_2026-08-06T16-04-29Z_served_mechanical.json. | A4 run0: served text says “you let them take column 2, row 1” while sentence 1 says the better move denies “the square they need” (c3r1) — board (4444332) shows the conceded square is c3r1; c2r1 is only a later completion square, so the served text tells the player the wrong square was conceded. | A4 run1: (i) “take the square at column 2, row 1, which opens their double threat” is board-false — c3r1 opens it (major threats appear only after move 7 = c3r1); (ii) “your four-in-a-row line from column 2 to column 5” is board-false for player 2 (c4r1, c5r1 are P1). Both claims are verbatim render-supplied. | A5 run1: A5b bites (player===2 AND boardState===“opening”); “keeps your four-in-a-row line … from being handed over” claims the 2nd player is building a win on a window that is dead for them, and there is no hold-the-line/toughest-defense frame. Render-supplied → render_bug per the A5 triage rule. Run0 passes A5b (“the tougher defense in column 3”). | A7b run0: “the square they need to start the four-in-a-row line running across the bottom” names no square (its [zone:opp-key-line] wrapper is line-shaped, not square-shaped), and the only square offered as the answer, c2r1, is the wrong object. | A7c run1: mechanism IS a double threat; the pivot that creates it (c3r1) is present in the text but credited to the better move, while the fork’s opening is attributed to c2r1 — the pivot is never identified as the pivot. The pivot WAS offered (render_decision.zones.aliases you-key-square = c3r1). | G5 both: two run-time aliases are board-false on their truthBoard “decision” — you-key-square (c3r1, “completing you’s four-in-a-row line”) and you-key-line (c2r1..c5r1, “the line you are playing for”); both sit in a window already holding two P1 discs. | G7 both: mechanical membership already fails — run0 emitted unoffered handle opp-key-line, run1 emitted unoffered term slug double_threat (render_decision.zones.terms is empty). Judgment half also fails run0: [zone:you-key-square] wraps “your own saving square on c3r1” inside a clause asserting the OPPONENT creates something, in a sentence that is grammatically broken (“create a … is no longer enough to matter”). annotationRepairs is [] on both runs, so G7c did not fire. | PROMPT-RECONSTRUCTION CAVEAT (Step 0b): assembleGroundedPrompt(buildReasonRenderModel(fv)) on TODAY’s code does NOT reproduce what this 2026-08-06 run saw — today’s prompt offers opp-key-square/opp-key-square-2/opp-key-line and says “the whole four-in-a-row line your OPPONENT is playing for”, and its L2 reads “let the opponent occupy column 3”. The stored render_decision (you-key-square/you-key-line, L2 “occupy c2r1”) is the run-time record, and run1’s emitted you-key-line handle exists only there, confirming the model saw the stored version. I graded against the stored render_decision per Step 0 and did NOT use the reconstructed prompt to charge the model — both render defects named above appear already FIXED in the current tree. | MODEL REGIME: gpt-5.4-mini, production-fidelity; no prompt_confusion bucket used — every failure is attributed to a render-layer field that is board-false, which survives a change of model.
